body: ## Problem The published docs currently generate at least one broken root-relative link from the docs index/sidebar content. Example rendered anchor: ```html What is a self-evolving repository? ``` That URL does not work on the docs site because the page lives under the docs namespace, e.g. `/docs/overview/what-is-self-evolving-repo`. The likely source is `.agent/docs/README.md`, which uses links like: ```md [What is a self-evolving repository?](overview/what-is-self-evolving-repo.md) ``` Those links are valid in the source repo, but when the README is synced/published as the docs index, Quartz resolves them as root-level `/overview/...` links instead of `/docs/overview/...`. ## Suggested resolution Please either: 1. Update the docs publishing/sync step to rewrite links from `.agent/docs/README.md` so published links resolve under `/docs/...`; or 2. Change the source docs/link structure so the generated site gets `/docs/overview/...` URLs. ## Also worth reconsidering Do we need `overview/what-is-self-evolving-repo.md` as a standalone page? It may be clearer to fold that conceptual explanation into the docs index (`.agent/docs/README.md`) and make the index the canonical "what is Sepo / self-evolving repo" entry point. If we do that, the broken link can be removed rather than fixed. ## Acceptance criteria - Clicking "What is a self-evolving repository?" from the generated docs no longer routes to `/overview/...`. - Either the link resolves correctly under `/docs/...`, or the standalone page is merged into the docs index and the nav/index link is removed/updated. - Similar root-level generated links from `.agent/docs/README.md` are checked and corrected.
title: Docs: fix generated overview links and reconsider standalone concept page
